And deleting completely everything about trustless payments oh, i see, that sounds like a big change Oh not really, it's a simplifying one You just remove stuff mostly and add a lookahead for builders. And can even give them negative issuance. It's a big change from the staking market perspective but from the specs/implementation point of view it's a simplifying one it is definitely a simplification of the protocol. changing the market sounds big and hard to champion Otoh it means going back to the status quo: stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost. The drop in issuance is IMO the only thing that is hard to get through > stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost Do you mean they sell via protocol only when favorable builder is selected and use mev boost otherwise? no, I mean sell via MEV boost exactly as it is today, off protocol. The point is that attesters (home stakers) do not need to be worried anymore about MEV and about proposing. And large pools can just take a percentage of their stake (say suppose today 15% of their income comes from proposals and 85% from attestations) then they'll move 15% of their stake to the builder slice and sell via Mev Boost exactly as today and they'll keep the status quo. If in addition we charge them (giving negative issuance to builders) then the computation is modified accordingly. excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: You just remove stuff mostly and add a lookahead for builders. And can even give them negative issuance. It's a big change from the staking market perspective but from the specs/implementation point of view it's a simplifying one

excerpts.author: m.kalinin

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Otoh it means going back to the status quo: stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost. The drop in issuance is IMO the only thing that is hard to get through

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
> stakers can allocate to the builder slice and sell JIT with mev boost

Do you mean they sell via protocol only when favorable builder is selected and use mev boost otherwise?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: no, I mean sell via MEV boost exactly as it is today, off protocol. The point is that attesters (home stakers) do not need to be worried anymore about MEV and about proposing. And large pools can just take a percentage of their stake (say suppose today 15% of their income comes from proposals and 85% from attestations) then they'll move 15% of their stake to the builder slice and sell via Mev Boost exactly as today and they'll keep the status quo. If in addition we charge them (giving negative issuance to builders) then the computation is modified accordingly.
